requirements.statement: Each declaration of background colour (background, background-color) on an element that can contain text is accompanied by a declaration of text colour (color), on the element or inherited from a parent.

citations.quote: chaque déclaration de couleur de fond (`background`, `background-color`), d’un élément susceptible de contenir du texte, est-elle accompagnée d’une déclaration de couleur de police (`color`) au moins, héritée d’un parent ?
Déterminer l’élément qui contient le texte et vérifier la présence d’une valeur calculée pour la propriété `color` de l’élément ;

routes.statement: A text colour is declared on the element or on one of its ancestors.

citations.quote: accompagnée d’une déclaration de couleur de police (`color`) au moins, héritée d’un parent

exceptions.statement: The browser's default colours, such as those of links, are not examined.

citations.quote: Retrouver dans le document les textes mis en couleur, à l’exception des couleurs par défaut (par exemple les liens, etc.) ;

rationale.text: The test asks that every declaration of background colour on an element that can contain text be accompanied by a text colour declared on the element or an ancestor. The methodology starts from the coloured texts of the page, leaves out default colours, and checks the colour of the element holding the text. A text colour may be accompanied in ways a reader could count or not, so the entry is not full. The methodology's selection step repeats the wording of test 10.5.1 (« textes mis en couleur »), and its step 2 asks for a computed value of color, which every rendered element has: read literally, it can pass, or never select, a paragraph with only a declared background-color and the default text colour, which the wording fails. Decision Q46 settles this: Fabien ruled that 10.5.2 follows its wording, and that the methodology's selection step, copied from 10.5.1, is not followed where it would pass a page the wording fails. One case is mechanical under the wording: an author declaration gives a visible background colour to a text's element or one of its ancestors, and no colour declaration accompanies it, so the text is drawn in the browser's default colour. The custom check looks for such a text and requires it to be surely in scope: ordinary visible text of two letters or more, exposed, outside shadow trees, in a generic or common system font, with nothing else painted under it, so the declared background is behind it. Its witness records the author background declaration that wins the cascade (the element, its style sheet or style attribute, its selector and its value), and rules out any author text colour applying to the element: it abstains when the chain holds any author or user declaration of color, whatever its value, or of -webkit-text-fill-color or the all shorthand, when an author rule colours the ::first-line or ::first-letter of an element of the chain, and when a user-agent rule gives the chain a colour (links, buttons, fields, mark, dialog), which covers the methodology's default-colour exception. It establishes where the text colour comes from, animations and transitions included, on the element and on every ancestor it inherits from: CSS keyframes, a CSS transition or an animation made by script can supply an author colour that no ordinary rule declares, paused, delayed or frozen by a forwards fill included, as Codex's re-check showed in Chrome with a paused animation setting color on a paragraph whose ordinary rules declare none. So the check abstains when any animation or transition targets the element, an ancestor or one of their pseudo-elements, whatever it animates, when any of them has a computed animation-name other than none, when a view transition is active, and when it cannot read the animations or the DevTools styles. This abstention is broad on purpose: it is easy to state and to verify, and it costs only claims. It also abstains on every case where the default text colour could be the author's declared intent: a background given as a CSS-wide keyword, currentcolor, a system colour such as Canvas, or light-dark(), a background that comes only from a presentational attribute, and a color-scheme other than normal. Under the wording the remaining witness fails under any reading: a declared background colour on an element that holds text, with no declaration of color on it or inherited from a parent. Its fault covers the route and the default-colour exception, so it means failure; it never answers no_fault, so the entry is fail_only. Scope is partial: it looks at texts, not at every element with a background declaration. No axe rule is tagged. Applicability is judgment, for the same reasons as test 10.5.1. Needs is empty.
